Scenario

A university wants a digital parking permit system. Students and staff can register vehicles, request parking permits, check available parking zones, and report parking issues. Security staff can verify permits and update violation records.

Task 1 — Requirements

Functional Requirements

  1. FR-1 Vehicle Registration. A student or staff member shall be able to register a vehicle by entering plate number, make, model, color, and owner ID. Duplicate plate numbers are rejected.
  2. FR-2 Permit Request. A registered user shall be able to submit a parking permit request, choosing zone (A/B/C/Visitor) and period (semester, annual, daily). The system returns a confirmation number.
  3. FR-3 Zone Availability Check. The system shall display real-time availability for each parking zone (free spots, capacity, and status: open / full / closed) before the user picks a zone.
  4. FR-4 Permit Verification by Security. Security staff shall be able to scan or enter a permit ID and immediately see whether the permit is valid, expired, suspended, or unknown, with the linked vehicle and owner.

Non-Functional Requirements

  1. NFR-1 Performance. Permit verification at security gates shall return a result within 2 seconds for 95% of requests under a load of 200 concurrent verifications.
  2. NFR-2 Security & Privacy. All personal data (owner ID, plate, address) shall be transmitted over TLS 1.2+, stored encrypted at rest, and access shall be limited by role (student, staff, security, admin).

Task 4 — Defect Analysis

Defect: "A valid parking permit is shown as expired during security verification."

ItemAnalysis
Defect categoryFunctional defect — incorrect business-logic output (date / time-zone calculation bug in permit verification).
SeverityHigh. A valid permit holder is wrongly flagged as expired, blocking legitimate users from parking and forcing manual security overrides. Not Critical (no crash) but breaks a core feature.
PriorityHigh / P1. Must be fixed in the next release. The defect runs on the security-gate path many times per day and is highly visible.
Possible root causeExpiry comparison most likely uses the server's local date while expiry_date is stored in UTC (or vice versa). Around the day boundary, today's date is still ≤ expiry in UTC but already > expiry after a naive local-date cast. Other candidates: off-by-one on inclusive/exclusive end date, or stale cached permit status not refreshed after renewal.
Regression testTC-06: after the fix, verify a permit whose expiry_date is in the future across multiple time-zone boundaries (just before midnight local, just after midnight local, and on the exact expiry day). Expected: status VALID in all three runs. Add this test to the regression suite so the bug cannot return.
